REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL — Manned guarding and mobile patrol services for stations and depots
Harbor County Transit Authority (fictional) · HCTA-SEC-2026-11

1. Introduction
Harbor County Transit Authority (fictional) invites proposals for: manned guarding and mobile patrol services for stations and depots.
Scope: 24/7 manned guarding at 3 depots and 9 stations, mobile patrols between sites, CCTV monitoring support and incident reporting, for an initial term of 3 years.

2. Timetable
Clarification questions close: 2026-11-18 at 16:00
Bidder briefing (online): 2026-11-21 at 14:00
Proposal submission deadline: 2026-12-02 at 12:00
Proposal validity: 90 days after the submission deadline
Planned contract start: 2027-01-15
All times are local time at the buyer's offices. Late proposals will not be considered.

3. Evaluation criteria
Proposals will be scored against the criteria and weightings below. Quality questions are scored from 0 to 5 and then weighted.
Q1 — Operational approach and post orders — 30% — How posts, patrols and CCTV support will be run and supervised around the clock.
Q2 — Officer licensing, vetting and training — 20% — Licensing status, vetting, initial and refresher training, including de-escalation.
Q3 — Incident management and reporting — 15% — Incident response, escalation, reporting times and use of technology.
Q4 — Transition and contingency — 10% — Mobilisation from the incumbent and cover for absence or major events.
P1 — Price — 25% — Total evaluated price from the price schedule.

4. Documents to be returned
Bidders shall return the following documents. A proposal missing any mandatory document may be rejected as non-compliant.
- Signed form of tender (Mandatory)
- Technical proposal answering Q1 to Q4 (max 25 pages) (Mandatory)
- Completed price schedule (Mandatory)
- Security business licence (Mandatory)
- Proof of insurance cover (Mandatory)
- Three client references (Mandatory)
- Sample patrol report (Optional)
- Organisation chart for the contract (Mandatory)

5. Instructions to bidders
Proposals shall be submitted in English through the buyer's e-procurement portal. Email submissions will not be accepted.
Questions shall be raised through the portal before the clarification deadline. Answers will be shared with all bidders without naming the bidder who asked.
Bidders shall not contact evaluators directly during the procurement. Canvassing will lead to exclusion.
The buyer is not bound to accept the lowest priced or any proposal and will not reimburse bid costs.

docs.label: Terms and conditions
pages:
TERMS AND CONDITIONS OF CONTRACT
Harbor County Transit Authority (fictional) · HCTA-SEC-2026-11

1. Definitions and interpretation
In these conditions, the Buyer means the contracting authority named above and the Contractor means the successful bidder.

2. Contractor obligations
2.1 Insurance. The contractor shall hold public liability insurance of at least USD 10,000,000 per occurrence and professional indemnity of at least USD 2,000,000.
2.2 Vetting. All officers shall pass a background check covering the previous 5 years before deployment.

3. Commercial terms
3.1 Payment. Invoices shall be submitted monthly in arrears with timesheets and will be paid within 30 days.
3.2 Subcontracting. Subcontracting of guarding posts is not permitted without prior written approval.

4. Termination
Either party may terminate for material breach that is not remedied within 30 days of written notice.
5. Governing law
The contract is governed by the law of the Buyer's jurisdiction.

docs.label: Technical specification
pages:
TECHNICAL SPECIFICATION
Harbor County Transit Authority (fictional) · HCTA-SEC-2026-11

1. Purpose
This specification sets out the minimum requirements for: manned guarding and mobile patrol services for stations and depots. 'Shall' means a mandatory requirement; 'should' means a desirable requirement that will be considered in scoring.

2. Requirements (part 1)
2.1 Coverage. The contractor shall provide 24-hour, 7-day manned guarding at each depot listed in Annex A, with no post left unattended during shift changes.
2.2 Patrols. Mobile patrol vehicles shall visit every station at least four times per night between 22:00 and 06:00, with each visit recorded electronically.
2.3 Licensing. Every officer shall hold a valid security licence for the role before deployment and carry it while on duty.

3. Requirements (part 2)
3.1 Training. Officers shall complete conflict de-escalation and first aid training before deployment and refresh it at least every 24 months.
3.2 Incidents. Serious incidents shall be reported by phone to the Authority's control room within 15 minutes and in writing within 24 hours.
3.3 Supervision. A shift supervisor shall be on duty at all times and shall make at least one welfare check per officer per shift.

4. Requirements (part 3)
4.1 Technology. The bidder should describe the guard-tour and reporting system used and how the Authority can access live data.
4.2 Contingency. The contractor shall be able to supply up to 10 additional officers within 12 hours for special events or emergencies.
4.3 Station procedures. Officers deployed at stations shall be trained in the Authority's evacuation procedures within their first week on site.

kb.title: Past proposal — Westfield Rail depots
kb.text: Post orders are written for each site and reviewed with the client every quarter. Shift handovers take place at the post, so no post is ever left unattended during a change of shift.

kb.title: Patrol operations
kb.text: Patrol vehicles follow randomised routes and record each site visit with an NFC checkpoint scan. Visit logs, timestamps and photos are available to the client the same night.

kb.title: Licensing register
kb.text: All 214 officers hold a valid licence for their role. Licence expiry dates are tracked and officers are stood down automatically 30 days before expiry unless renewed.

kb.title: Training programme
kb.text: Initial training covers conflict de-escalation, first aid, report writing and customer care. Refreshers are delivered every 18 months.

kb.title: Incident escalation procedure
kb.text: Serious incidents are called through to the client control room within 10 minutes by the supervisor, followed by a written report within 12 hours.

kb.title: Supervision and welfare
kb.text: A mobile supervisor is on duty on every shift and makes at least two welfare checks per officer per shift, in person or by radio.

kb.title: Guard-tour technology
kb.text: Our guard-tour platform records checkpoints, incidents and photos in real time. Clients get read-only dashboard access and a weekly PDF summary.

kb.title: Surge capacity
kb.text: A relief pool of vetted officers allows us to provide up to 15 extra officers within 8 hours for events or emergencies.

kb.title: Insurance summary
kb.text: Public liability USD 15,000,000 per occurrence; professional indemnity USD 5,000,000.

kb.title: Vetting standard
kb.text: Every officer completes a background check covering at least the previous 5 years, with gaps explained and verified, before deployment.

bullets.text: Site-specific post orders reviewed with the Authority every quarter.

All officers hold a valid licence; expiry dates are tracked and officers are stood down 30 days before expiry unless renewed.
De-escalation and first aid before deployment, refreshed every 18 months — inside the 24-month requirement.

Live guard-tour dashboard with read-only access for the Authority and a weekly summary.
Relief pool able to supply up to 15 extra officers within 8 hours, above the 10 officers in 12 hours required.
Mobile supervisor on every shift with at least two welfare checks per officer.
Hourly rates include wages, overheads and margin; overtime and holiday rates are capped at 1.5 times the standard rate.
